counterexample: Observed timeout witness: a one-process server registers process.on("SIGTERM",()=>{}) and continues answering. After a local CLI error, the unchanged verifier reaches cleanup and waits indefinitely for that process; the cited fixture still answered after the bounded 12s observation until forced kill. A otherwise fully functional SQLite app can use the same slow/draining shutdown handler: instruction.md:9 and integration.md:3-10 require a single process, health and durable restart behavior but specify no SIGTERM shutdown deadline, so its product compliance does not give this wait a bound. Broken-app plausibility check: the same indexed fixture observed restart_app report success after 6.0878s while old PID7 still answered and replacement PID68 failed EADDRINUSE. A memory-only app retaining the old process could therefore appear persistent if that success is trusted; no actual criterion pass is claimed. Conforming-alternative workload risk, not a measured failure: a legitimate multi-screen wizard may need substantially more browser discovery/actions for P1-P10/B1-B6 and four polish recovery branches than the compact golden scripts; missing full judge timing leaves timeout-caused zero observations unresolved even though budget arithmetic passes.
